## Overview
- Goal: serve high-quality, low-latency responses during live technical interviews.
- Inputs: conversational text, audio (user speech), and screen data (e.g., code editor or shared screen cues).
- Output: concise text replies; optionally aligned with timestamps for UI display.
- Design priorities: sub-1s end-to-end latency, graceful scaling with many concurrent meetings, and safe handling of user data.

## Workload assumptions (to size and test)
- Concurrent meetings: plan for hundreds of connected meetings in peak hours; size capacity per region based on forecast (e.g., p99 concurrent load).
- Event rate: bursts around question/answer turns; audio chunks ~0.5–1.0s, screen snapshots every few seconds (configurable).
- Latency targets: <300–500ms per hop (ingest → preproc → model → postproc), keeping end-to-end <2s for most turns; <1s stretch goal for short answers.
- Token/sequence budget: keep prompts lean; truncate/summary long histories to keep context windows within budget and stable latency.
